process_area.title: Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Category Managers, Pricing (links to VS-01.2/VS-57), Merchandising Finance (links to VS-101.3), Master Data (links to VS-29)
fields.Trigger: Cost change (W3414); margin-plan variance (links to VS-101.3); quarterly pricing review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-analyze of "analyze the cost change" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "update shelf labels" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track realized pass-through vs decision, measure margin retention, and report…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-70 (ensure commodity exposure & hedge accounting accuracy.)
- operational: disciplined margin modeling and competitor check (W3420); operational: competitor sensitivity (W3420)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-pass-through risk**: Absorbing cost erodes margin/EBITDA (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by disciplined margin modeling and competitor check (W3420)
- **Over-pass-through risk**: Passing through beyond market harms price-competitiveness (links to VS-57) and volume; mitigated by competitor sensitivity (W3420)
System Touchpoints: - Price management (links to VS-01.2/W40/W107); shelf labels (links to VS-08 W63); ecommerce price (links to VS-10/VS-65/VS-95); margin/OTB (links to VS-101.3/W3286); DTI compliance (links to VS-22/W468)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Pricing analyze the cost change (from indexed formula W3414, vendor surcharge, landed cost links to VS-02.2, or hedge settlement W3413) and model the maintained-margin impact (links to VS-101 W3286); determine the pass-through decision: full pass-through, partial (absorb/share), or hold price

Category Managers/Pricing execute the SRP/cost change per VS-01.2/W40 (price hierarchy, authority matrix links to VS-36), update shelf labels (links to VS-08 W63/W181), ecommerce/marketplace prices (links to VS-10/VS-65/VS-95 price parity), and comply with DTI price-tag/price-freeze rules (links to VS-22/W468); respect OTB/markdown-budget controls (links to VS-101 W3283/W3285)

Merchandising Finance track realized pass-through vs decision, measure margin retention, and report commodity-driven price/cost variance to the merchandise P&A (links to VS-101 W3288) and margin analytics (W3419); feed learning to the next decision

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Category Managers, Pricing (links to VS-01.2), Treasury (links to VS-18), Supply (links to VS-02), Marketing (links to VS-14)
fields.Trigger: Market shock (W3407); sudden cost surge; supply disruption (links to VS-69/VS-02.3)

workflows.name: Rapid Commodity-Shock Price Response & Margin Recovery

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "Treasury/Procurement alert the rapid-response group on a commodity shock" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-communication of "communicate to stores/ecommerce" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Merchandising/Marketing manage customer communication" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: pre-defined triggers and authority; operational: measured, value-driven response
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: Slow response locks in loss; mitigated by pre-defined triggers and authority

- **Reputational risk**: Visible opportunistic pricing during a crisis (e.g., post-typhoon links to VS-69) attracts DTI/consumer backlash (links to VS-22/W469); mitigated by measured, value-driven response
System Touchpoints: - Price management (links to VS-01.2); hedge/buy (links to W3410/W3412); inventory (links to VS-05); competitor (links to VS-57); comms (links to VS-14.3)

steps.activity: Treasury/Procurement alert the rapid-response group on a commodity shock (e.g., +20% steel, oil spike, cement allocation); quantify exposure impact (W3404), hedge coverage (W3412), inventory position (links to VS-05), and competitor posture (links to VS-57)

VP Merchandising/Pricing decide the price response: emergency SRP adjustment (links to VS-01.2), temporary surcharge, promo hold, or hold price using inventory/hedge buffer; execute via VS-01.2/W40 within authority, respect DTI rules (links to VS-22/W468), and communicate to stores/ecommerce

Merchandising/Marketing manage customer communication (links to VS-14.3) and competitor response (links to VS-57); Treasury execute emergency hedge/buy (links to W3410/W3412) if warranted; track margin recovery and report to executives (links to VS-33.2) and the post-event review (W3416)

fields.Participants: Merchandising Finance, Category Managers, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Treasury (links to VS-18)
fields.Trigger: Monthly close (links to VS-17.1/W9A); weekly P&A (links to VS-101 W3288)

workflows.name: Maintained-Margin Impact Analysis & Commodity Variance Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Merchandising Finance report commodity-margin variance to the weekly P&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-70 (ensure commodity exposure & hedge accounting accuracy.)
- operational: rigorous decomposition; operational: weekly cadence
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution-error risk**: Mis-attributing FX/mix/freight as commodity distorts the variance; mitigated by rigorous decomposition
- **Latency risk**: Late variance delays corrective action; mitigated by weekly cadence
System Touchpoints: - Margin/cost analytics (links to VS-85/VS-101.3); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); GL close (links to VS-17.1); treasury MTM (links to VS-18)

steps.activity: Merchandising Finance decompose the maintained-margin variance (links to VS-101 W3286) into drivers: commodity cost (W3401), FX (links to VS-18.3), freight (links to VS-06/VS-87), markdown (links to VS-101 W3285), mix, shrink (links to VS-23), and hedge outcome (W3413); isolate the commodity-driven component

Merchandising Finance compare realized commodity cost vs the merchandise plan assumption (links to VS-101 W3281/W3286), the hedge offset (W3416), and the pass-through outcome (W3417); quantify net commodity impact on GM% and EBITDA

Merchandising Finance report commodity-margin variance to the weekly P&A (links to VS-101 W3288), monthly finance close (links to VS-17.1), FP&A (links to VS-17.4), and the commodity-risk review (W3423); feed to forecast reforecast (links to VS-101 W3288) and strategy adjustment (W3416)

fields.Participants: Pricing Manager, Category Managers, Competitive Intelligence (links to VS-57/VS-33.3), Merchandising Finance
fields.Trigger: Pass-through decision (W3417); quarterly competitive review (links to VS-57)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "posture per category" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Pricing/Merchandising decide and execute the category pass-through posture, monitor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: feasibility assessment and tactical flexibility; operational: margin-vs-volume modeling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Share-loss risk**: Passing through while competitors hold price loses share; mitigated by feasibility assessment and tactical flexibility
- **Margin-sacrifice risk**: Holding price to match competitors erodes margin; mitigated by margin-vs-volume modeling
System Touchpoints: - Competitive price intelligence (links to VS-57); market research (links to VS-44/VS-33.3); price management (links to VS-01.2); margin model (links to VS-101 W3286)

steps.activity: Pricing/Competitive Intelligence assess competitor pricing and pass-through behavior on commodity-exposed categories using competitive price intelligence (links to VS-57 W130/W329) and market research (links to VS-44/VS-33.3): who has passed through, by how much, and the elasticity signal

Category Managers/Pricing model pass-through feasibility: price elasticity (links to VS-58 promo elasticity), volume/market-share impact, competitor retaliation risk, and the margin-vs-volume trade-off; recommend the pass-through posture per category

Pricing/Merchandising decide and execute the category pass-through posture, monitor competitor and volume response, and adjust (links to VS-57 tactical response W329); feed learning to the margin model (links to VS-101 W3286) and the next review

fields.Participants: Procurement Director, Category Managers, Vendor, Finance (links to VS-15/VS-39), Legal (links to VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: Market price drop not reflected in vendor price; vendor overcharge; formula asymmetry

workflows.name: Vendor Recovery / Claim & Commodity Savings Capture

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify vendor-recovery opportunities" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Finance capture the recovery" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: active monitoring and benchmarking (W3403); operational: data-based, contract-grounded negotiation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Savings-leakage risk**: Market drops not claimed = margin leakage (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by active monitoring and benchmarking (W3403)
- **Dispute-escalation risk**: Claims damage vendor relationship; mitigated by data-based, contract-grounded negotiation
System Touchpoints: - Vendor contract/AP (links to VS-03.3/VS-15.1); rebate (links to VS-39); dispute (links to VS-90/W244); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement identify vendor-recovery opportunities: market price drops (W3403) not passed through, formula-asymmetry overcharge, vendor invoice error vs contract (links to VS-03.3/W3411), and unclaimed savings; quantify the recovery

Procurement negotiate and claim the recovery (credit memo links to VS-15.1/W7.9b, rebate/adjustment links to VS-39, contract amendment links to VS-03.3); resolve disputes (links to VS-90/W244) with Legal support (links to VS-100.3) as needed

Finance capture the recovery (credit posting links to VS-17.1/VS-15.1), validate against expectation, and report commodity savings capture to the review (W3416) and vendor scorecard (links to VS-67); feed systemic asymmetry to contract redesign (W3411)

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Category Managers, Merchandising Finance (links to VS-101.3), Clearance (links to VS-64/VS-05.3)
fields.Trigger: Commodity thesis invalidation (W3410); aged strategic inventory; margin-plan variance (W3419)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "identify commodity-inventory at risk" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "attribute to the commodity decision (W3410)" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: tighter forward-buy discipline (W3410) and OTB control; operational: timely clearance decision
Pain Points / Risks: - **Markdown-erosion risk**: Clearing invalidated forward-buys erodes margin (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by tighter forward-buy discipline (W3410) and OTB control
- **Holding-cost risk**: Holding aged commodity stock ties up working capital (links to VS-105); mitigated by timely clearance decision
System Touchpoints: - Markdown budget (links to VS-101 W3285); clearance (links to VS-64); transfer (links to VS-05.2); disposition (links to VS-05.3/VS-32.3)

steps.activity: Merchandising Finance/Category Managers identify commodity-inventory at risk: forward-bought stock where the price thesis invalidated (W3410), aged strategic inventory, or commodity price-drop making current cost above market; quantify the markdown exposure vs the markdown budget (links to VS-101 W3285)

Category Managers/VP Merchandising decide clearance/markdown action within the markdown budget (links to VS-101 W3285) and authority: clearance event (links to VS-64.2), transfer (links to VS-05.2), vendor return (links to VS-32.2/VS-90), or hold; execute via VS-01.2/VS-64

Merchandising Finance track realized markdown vs commodity exposure, attribute to the commodity decision (W3410), and feed learning to the forward-buy discipline (W3410) and margin analytics (W3419); clear residual per disposition (links to VS-05.3/VS-32.3)

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, Procurement, Merchandising Finance, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), BI (links to VS-28.1), CFO

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review with Merchandising, Finance, and Supply" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report commodity-risk performance and outlook to the executive committee" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: integrated dashboard; operational: single source and audit sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-silo risk**: Commodity data scattered across treasury/procurement/finance; mitigated by integrated dashboard
- **Disclosure-inconsistency risk**: Risk disclosures inconsistent with financials; mitigated by single source and audit sign-off
System Touchpoints: - BI/dashboard (links to VS-28.1); treasury/risk (links to VS-18/VS-21.2); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Treasury/BI publish the commodity-risk dashboard: exposure map (W3401), market prices/trend (W3403), sensitivity/VaR (W3404), hedge/mitigation status and MTM (W3412/W3413), pass-through outcome (W3417/W3419), and net margin impact; monthly full + event flash

CFO/Treasury/Procurement conduct the monthly commodity-risk review with Merchandising, Finance, and Supply: variance to plan, mitigation effectiveness (W3416), risk/issues, and corrective actions; assign owners and SLAs

CFO report commodity-risk performance and outlook to the executive committee (links to VS-33.2) and Audit Committee/Board (links to VS-36); align with margin/EBITDA narrative (links to VS-101.3/VS-17.4) and ensure disclosure consistency (links to VS-17)

fields.Participants: CFO, Treasury Manager, Procurement Director, Risk (links to VS-21.2), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Board (links to VS-36)
fields.Trigger: Annual policy/audit cycle (links to VS-21/VS-36); post-event review

workflows.name: Commodity Risk Policy Compliance, Audit & Continuous Improvement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Treasury/CFO maintain the commodity-risk policy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review commodity-risk controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "post-event and continuous-improvement reviews" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-549 (ensure controlled execution — Input-Cost Pass-Through, Margin Protection & Risk Analytics (PA-106.3).)
- operational: SoD, authority limits, and audit; operational: annual review and event triggers
Pain Points / Risks: - **Control-bypass risk**: Unauthorized/speculative hedging outside policy; mitigated by SoD, authority limits, and audit
- **Policy-staleness risk**: Outdated policy misaligns with market/business change; mitigated by annual review and event triggers
System Touchpoints: - Policy repository (links to VS-186); ERM (links to VS-21.2); audit (links to VS-21); board reporting (links to VS-36); treasury policy (links to VS-18 W322)

steps.activity: Treasury/CFO maintain the commodity-risk policy: hedge authority and limits (links to W3406/W3409), indexed-contract standards (W3411), forward-buy/strategic-inventory limits (links to VS-101 OTB), pass-through governance (W3417), and accounting/tax compliance (W3413/links to VS-79); align to ERM (links to VS-21.2) and treasury policy (links to VS-18 W322)

Internal Audit review commodity-risk controls: SoD over hedging (links to W3412/W3413), authority compliance, formula integrity (W3414/W3421), disclosure accuracy, and policy adherence; feed findings to remediation (links to VS-21 issue tracking)

CFO/Treasury conduct post-event and continuous-improvement reviews (links to VS-30 innovation/automation where relevant), capture lessons, update policy/process, and report governance and compliance to the Board (links to VS-36); ensure ongoing alignment with the risk appetite and business strategy
